sentences.text: Gracilisuchus is an extinct genus of tiny pseudosuchians from the Late Triassic of Argentina.
The only species, G. stipanicicorum, belongs to the clade Suchia, which is close to the ancestry of crocodylomorphs.
The largest skull measures slightly over 9 cm in length, and the largest femur is roughly 8 cm long.
A scleral ring exists within the eye socket, where the ossicles contact but do not overlap each other.
A small, triangular postparietal bone is present.
Gracilisuchus possessed eight vertebrae in its neck region.
The lower end of Gracilisuchus's upper arm bone was 2.5 times wider than its shaft.
Gracilisuchus had two rows of bony plates called osteoderms running from behind its skull over its neck and torso.
Gracilisuchus differed from other rauisuchians by lacking an ossification at the back of the top of the skull and a fenestra between the premaxilla and maxilla.
Alfred Romer first described both the genus and the species in 1972 in the journal Breviora.
The holotype specimen is now housed at the Museum of Paleontology at the National University of La Rioja with the number PULR 08.
The species name G. stipanicicorum honors the work of Pedro and Maria Stipanicic in the stratigraphy and paleobotany of the Triassic period.
Romer initially reconstructed Gracilisuchus as a facultative biped, though this interpretation was based on material later reassigned.
Romer classified Gracilisuchus as a clear relative of Ornithosuchus based on skull and skeletal similarities.
Arthur Cruickshank removed Gracilisuchus from Ornithosuchidae because it possessed a "crocodile-normal" ankle joint unlike other members of the family.
Brinkman tentatively placed Gracilisuchus closer to crocodile-line archosaurs like Erythrosuchidae and Rauisuchidae rather than Ornithosuchids.

Phylogenetic analysis recovered Gracilisuchus as a member of Suchia, defined by a "crocodile-normal" ankle and other traits, a move Paul Sereno formalized in 1991 to define the contents of the group Suchia.
In 1994, Lars Juul placed Gracilisuchus inside Paracrocodylomorpha as the sister taxon of Postosuchus.
A 2004 analysis by Benton found Gracilisuchus to be the sister taxon of the Phytosauria.
A 2014 analysis by Richard Butler named a group containing Gracilisuchus, Turfanosuchus, and Yonghesuchus as Gracilisuchidae.
Its time range is estimated from 241.464 to 237 million years ago during the Ladinian.
Uranium-lead dating of Chañares deposits in 2016 indicated an early Carnian age of 236 to 234 million years.
Scientists have not reached a consensus on the evolutionary relationships between Gracilisuchus and other crurotarsans.
